items: Preschool children (2-5y) show developmental regression, separation anxiety, and magical thinking attributing divorce to their own behavior (Dulcan p.628, DSM p.218)
School-age children (6-11y) show overt grief, loyalty conflicts, reunification fantasies, and academic decline (Dulcan p.628)
Adolescents (12-18y) present with anger, moral condemnation, parentification, and externalizing risk behaviors (Dulcan p.625, p.628)
Adoption disclosure is recommended before age 3-5; adolescents experience dual identity integration and search for birth parents (Dulcan p.622, p.893)
RAD (F94.1) presents with emotional withdrawal, minimal comfort seeking/responding, and limited positive affect (DSM p.295-296)
DSED (F94.2) presents with disinhibited social familiarity with strangers, lack of checking back, and lack of hesitation (DSM p.298-299)
key_numbers: 2-5 years: preschool age group showing regression and magical thinking (Dulcan p.628)
9 months: minimum developmental age required for RAD and DSED diagnosis (DSM p.296, p.299)
5 years: maximum age threshold for RAD symptom onset (DSM p.296)

items: Chronic interparental conflict is the strongest predictor of child psychiatric morbidity, exceeding the impact of divorce itself (Dulcan p.628, p.631)
Parental alienation involves psychological splitting and borrowed scenarios, distinguished from realistic estrangement due to actual abuse (Dulcan p.629)
Adoptees have elevated rates of ODD, CD, ADHD, and FASD/ND-PAE due to genetic risks, prenatal toxic exposure, and institutional deprivation (Dulcan p.121, p.209, p.541-542, DSM p.918)
Foster youth experience placement instability leading to complex trauma, disorganized attachment, and dissociative symptoms (Dulcan p.520, p.632-633, DSM p.307)
key_numbers: 50% of children in foster care have a diagnosed psychiatric disorder (StahlKids p.16, p.488)
90% of youth in residential treatment centers (RTCs) experienced complex trauma or polyvictimization (StahlKids p.16, p.489, Dulcan p.518, p.520)

first_line: Trauma-Informed Care (TIC) and environmental stabilization (StahlKids p.16, p.489)
Child-Parent Psychotherapy (CPP) for infants and young children with trauma or foster care history (Dulcan p.308, p.357)
Divorce mediation and co-parenting counseling (Dulcan p.628, p.646)
second_line: Interpersonal Psychotherapy for Depressed Adolescents (IPT-A) targeting role transitions and disputes (Dulcan p.955-965)
Wraparound services and Intensive In-Home Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Services (IICAPS) (Dulcan p.1000-1012)
Monotherapy with 'Start Low, Go Slow' titration when medication is clinically indicated for confirmed psychiatric disorders (StahlKids p.16, p.491)
key_side_effects: Metabolic side effects including weight gain, dyslipidemia, and hyperglycemia from atypical antipsychotics (StahlKids p.109, p.500)
Sedation, extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS), and hyperprolactinemia (StahlKids p.109)
treatment.monitoring: Regular monitoring of weight, height, blood pressure, blood glucose, lipid profile, and metabolic parameters (StahlKids p.109, p.500)

items: Froma Walsh's Family Resilience Framework comprises Belief Systems, Organizational Patterns, and Communication Processes (Dulcan p.623-624, p.633-634)
Best Interests of the Child standard governs forensic custody and child welfare evaluations (Dulcan p.645-646, Syllabus p.39)
Dual Agency Prohibition strictly forbids treating clinicians from performing forensic custody evaluations (Dulcan p.644, p.648)
Written informed consent from BOTH legal guardians is required for treatment in high-conflict divorce (StahlKids p.16, p.109, Dulcan p.646)
Prohibition of chemical restraints forbids using psychotropics for non-specific behavior control in foster youth (StahlKids p.16, p.292, p.491)
key_numbers: 3 core domains in Walsh's Family Resilience Framework (Dulcan p.623-624)
7 years: minimum age for obtaining child informed assent (StahlKids p.16, p.109, Dulcan p.689)

high_yield: Chronic high interparental conflict is a stronger predictor of child psychiatric morbidity than divorce itself (Dulcan p.628, p.631).
Parental alienation presents with psychological splitting and borrowed scenarios, whereas realistic estrangement stems from actual abuse or neglect (Dulcan p.629).
RAD (F94.1) is an internalizing disorder that improves rapidly in a nurturing environment; DSED (F94.2) is an externalizing disorder that persists even in high-quality care (DSM p.297, p.300).
Both RAD and DSED require a minimum developmental age of 9 months and evidence of severe social neglect/insufficient care (DSM p.296, p.299).
Using antipsychotics or mood stabilizers as 'chemical restraints' for non-specific behavior control in foster youth is strictly prohibited (StahlKids p.16, p.292, p.491).
Treating clinicians are strictly prohibited from providing forensic custody evaluations due to dual agency conflict of interest (Dulcan p.644, p.648).

Psychiatric or pharmacological treatment in high-conflict divorce requires written informed consent from BOTH legal guardians regardless of physical custody ratio (StahlKids p.16, p.109, Dulcan p.646).
